comment: I'm not sure why Zylkin isn't talked about more, I took him first semester freshman year and I really liked him. I don't love economics but he made it easy to follow and gave opportunities for points back on exams. A lot of people I know in Bschool recommend him for any higher level classes too.

Great Professor and would definitely recommend, especially for someone like myself who had no prior knowledge of econ. He provides a very clear study guide for each test, which his exams follow closely. He provided a ton of resources and was always available outside of class and exams were very fair. Office hours were a bit awkward one-on-one.

I LOVED Prof. Zylkin! He is on your side and wants you to do well, but you have to put in the effort. I'm not interested in Econ, he made the subject interesting enough that I didn't hate the class. His lectures are clear but he tends to talk about concepts over and over again, which could sometimes get boring. Homework & exam grades were fair.

I enjoyed Professor Zylkin's class. He was pretty awkward but a nice and caring guy. I felt sometimes like he was speaking down to me in office hours but he was a wonderful lecturer. I learned a lot and he knows what he is talking about so I would definitely take him for an introductory econ course.

Zylkin is the accessible professor iv had at UR. He responds very quickly and is always happy to meet and help with material. Attendance is mandatory to understand material and the exams and homework are quite difficult.

Professor Zylkin is the most underrated econ professor. His lectures are easy to digest and interactive. Your grade consists of 2 midterms, a final, and homework assignments that are super easy. He'll drop your lowest test grade at the end of the class. He regularly holds office hours and big review sessions before exams and will give you snacks !!
Office hours are a bit awkward but if u try to communicate with email he gives you the perfect response.

Zylkin doesn't get the love he should, what a guy. He is very invested in his students, and tries his best to dumb down every single concept in the class. I've never emailed him and not heard back in 20 minutes even past 10pm. He also answers questions that we write to him on index cards including who's gonna win the prem which i find kinda cute.

Zylkin is very nice and a great lecturer. The class was fascinating, but provided a good challenge conceptually. There was a good mix of math and theory, monetary and trade policy, and papers and tests. lots of writing assignments and quizzes, but overall a doable amount of work. very friendly, but grades tough.

Professor Zylkin clearly understands what he teaches, but sometimes is repetitive to the point of confusion. Normally doesn't teach this class. Very accessible outside of class and cares about your learning; however, his grading system can be discouraging.

Econ 101: you can tell his is enthusiastic but can't dumb down concepts for us. To do well you need to watch his recorded lectures, read the textbook and go over his practice exams. The homework doesn't help so just ignore them. He's kinda awkward one on one but that's the only time when you actually learn the material. rent the textbook!

Very nice professor and accessible outside of class. You really notice that he is passionate about his subject. Most concepts are explained in videos he recorded which makes his expectations very clear. Studying these and practicing with quizzes are enough to get you in the A/B range and you will also genuinely understand the subject!

Offered optional review sessions before exams. Also provided note outlines, study guides, and extra credit. He sometimes struggled with dumbing down concepts. However, it's clear he wants students to succeed. Very accessible and always seeking student feedback to improve his class. He can be awkward, but he's a good guy and passionate about econ.

Prof Z might just be the best professor I've had at UR, and that's saying something. He cares so much about his students and really wants them to understand Econ. He always had like 3 hour long optional review sessions before tests and frequent office hours. His tests were definitely a challenge but I can say for sure I learned econ really well.

Professor Zylkin is super organized in the way he explains concepts and writes notes (he provides an outline for every class). He is clear with what he expects from students and rewards those who make an effort, as he is super accessible outside of class. He is clearly passionate about the subject and is hands down the best teacher I have had!!!

Prof Z cares deeply about his students and believes in every single one of them. I struggled with Econ a lot, and he made an effort to meet with me every week to try to help me understand it. He even held review sessions the nights before tests! He has a hard time rewording his explanations which made simple concepts more difficult to understand.
Love him as a professor, but teaches the material in a harder way than it actually is and I ended up having to reteach myself everything for the exams. Only 3 exams and a project.

One of the best econ professors! As someone who didn't take econ in highschool he did his upmost best to make sure we could succeed in his class. Whether it was hosting extra office hours, implementing our feedback, extra credit, AND EVEN letting us retake our exam. You will not find someone else who deeply cares for his students. TAKE HIS CLASS!!!
Makes complex material easy to understand and is extremely fair in terms of homework and grading. Listen in class, ask questions, and study for the exams and you will do well.

take this professor if you're still undecided about going to the business major. One of the few professors who can understand that his subject is not the most important in the world. Very humble, always willing to learn and improve his lectures.
the nicest professor ever. Truly wants all of his students to succeed. Outlines are really helpful.
Sometimes his explanations are a bit confusing. Dr. Zylkin is one of the nicest professors of the B school who wants all of his students to succeed.

Prof Z is such a genuinely interested professor. He takes time out of class to explain problems and hosts extra study sessions before midterms and such. This was my favorite class and I developed such an interest in economics through prof z. Grades are also not hard, just do the homework sets and go to study sessions.

Zylkin's class wasn't extremely interesting but he seemed genuinely excited about the material which always helps. Very clear and concise in his lectures and assignments. He really wants his students to succeed and enjoy his class. Easy A if you pay attention half the time and do the homework which isn't very hard at all.

Zylkin is a solid professor and is very intelligent. His expectations are clear and the material is interesting. There's a one page, single-spaced paper due about every week on a current event based on articles he gives you. The quizzes and midterm are mostly graphical. Then there's also a debate and a final paper. Great class all around.

His lectures have a lot of passion, although his pace is quite fast. But, he provides a ton of study materials and outlines to make exam cramming easy and efficient. Textbook is optional, everything else given in class is enough to get by textbook free. Overall, he's a a great prof that makes the content easy, and adds pinches of fun!

Class requires more work than I was expecting. Quizzes and discussion questions (which you have to write at least 1.5 pages to do well on) basically every week. The textbooks were completely unnecessary and I could've done the same without them. Very smart professor but hard at conveying what he's looking for.

Nice guy. A bit awkward outside of class. Almost entirely lecture based, textbook not really necessary. Kind of teacher that explains the concepts in the way that make sense to him, but not to the student and doesn't know how to explain it in another way. He is clear in assignments. Take if you want little work and a good grade

Very Lecture heavy professor who tends to confuse students about concepts. Textbook that was nearly 200 dollars does not correlate with the coursework at all and the tests are rather challenging. Wish I had a professor who was a little more straightforward and put emphasis on a textbook.

Lecture heavy, over time this class gets increasingly boring, he has a hard time explaining things and fully answering the questions asked by students. The professor is accessible outside and his office hours are pretty long and students can also make appointments.

Awesome professor who gives great lectures, is funny, and is always eager to connect absolutely everything to industry. Everything is presented in lecture formats w/ online assignments for interactive reinforcement. Only gives 3 major tests + group research project, so watch out. Optional textbook is optional; never used it. 100% would take again!
